reproduction_target: Functional-genomics analysis of trans-QTL effects on 3D genome contacts in mouse ESCs from B6/D2 congenic strains: ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq (H3K27ac, H3K9me3) read processing (trim/align/dedup/peak-call/count/differential), genome-browser track generation, restriction-enzyme HiChIP processing (HiC-Pro -> hichipper -> diffloop/DESeq2 differential loops), Dovetail MNase HiChIP processing (bwa -> pairtools -> samtools -> FitHiChIP -> diffloop/edgeR differential loops), and a RAD-framework spatial enrichment test in R. Wet-lab work (congenic mouse breeding and MiniMUGA genotyping, ESC derivation/culture, ATAC/ChIP/HiChIP library preparation and sequencing, 3C-qPCR) is out of computational-reproduction scope and counted in W.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool from the Methods subsections 'ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq data processing', 'HiChIP data processing and analysis' (both the restriction-enzyme and Dovetail MNase branches), and 'Spatial Enrichment Analysis'. bwa appears twice at two different pinned versions (0.7.5 for browser-track bigwigs, 0.7.18 for the Dovetail branch) and is therefore counted as two steps. The diffloop-based differential-loop calling appears twice (DESeq2 for the RE branch, edgeR for the Dovetail branch) and is likewise counted twice. The paper contains NO code-availability statement and NO repository link of any kind (full-text scan for github/gitlab/bitbucket/zenodo/figshare/osf/codeocean/dryad returned only the picard documentation URL github.io/picard/, which is upstream tool documentation, not an author artifact). Because most steps are command-line tools with an exact version pin, the code axis is scored 1 (reconstructable from prose) where the invocation and its parameters are stated, and 0 where the analysis is custom or the invocation is underspecified.

steps.label: Illumina adaptor trimming of ChIP reads with Trimmomatic version 0.39
Alignment to mm10 modified to incorporate known D2 variants from Mouse Genomes Project Database REL-1505, using hisat2 version 2.2.1
Duplicate-read removal with Picard Tools version 2.0.1
Per-sample peak calling with MACS version 1.4.2 (H3K27ac and H3K9me3)
Read-count generation across all samples over the previously published 'peakome' open-chromatin set (ref. 28) with bedtools version 2.9.2
TMM normalization + log2 transform and differential histone-modification analysis with edgeR version 3.34.1 (R/RStudio version 4.1)
bwa version 0.7.5 alignment with MAPQ<30 / unmapped / secondary / QC-fail / duplicate / supplementary filtering, and bigwig generation for browser tracks
Genome-browser track visualization with karyoploteR version 1.20.3

Restriction-enzyme HiChIP read processing with HiC-Pro v2.11.4 (N_CPU=4, SORT_RAM=768M, REFERENCE_GENOME=mm10, LIGATION_SITE=GATCGATC, MIN_FRAG_SIZE=30, MAX_FRAG_SIZE=100000, MIN_INSERT_SIZE=30, MAX_INSERT_SIZE=600)
Long-range interaction calling with hichipper v0.7.8b0 using the H3K27ac ChIP-seq peaks generated in this paper

RE-branch differential-interaction analysis: PET import + TMM normalization in diffloop v1.22.0 (R 4.1), anchors unmerged, interactions <5,000 bp filtered, FDR 0.01 p-adjust, >=4 reads in >=2 samples, DESeq2 within diffloop, DI cutoff FDR<0.2
Dovetail MNase HiChIP: alignment to mm10 with bwa v0.7.18 following Dovetail HiChIP Loop Calling docs (readthedocs Revision 8f2e0b16)
Recording/sorting valid ligation events, PCR-duplicate removal, .pairs and bam generation with pairtools version 1.1.2
Final bam creation/indexing and QC thresholds (no-dup pairs >50%, >=~20% cis >1 kb, >2% reads within 1 kb of ChIP peak centers) with Samtools version 1.19.2
Loop calling with FitHiChIP version 11.0 (peak-to-peak, bin 2500, lower distance 10000, upper distance 2000000, coverage-bias regression, merge filtering option 1, q-value 0.01, mm10 chrom sizes)

Dovetail-branch differential-interaction analysis: peak-to-peak import into R 4.1, diffloop version 1.22.0 FDR 0.01 p-adjust, >=4 reads in >=2 samples, PET normalization, edgeR version 3.34.1 differential calling at FDR<0.2

Spatial Enrichment Analysis: adapted RAD framework (ref. 68) - signed strand-specific TSS-to-peak distances binned in 100 kb intervals over -500 kb..+500 kb, binom.test in R (alternative='greater', p = M_focal/N_total), Benjamini-Hochberg correction; ESC-expressed gene background per ref. 28

headline.static_readiness: 0/17 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 13/17 computational steps reach RI at the prose level and 4 fall to NI. The RI ceiling is set by the code axis: there is no code repository, no scripts, no notebooks and no code-availability statement anywhere in the paper, so every step is at best reconstructable-from-prose (code=1), never public+exact (code=2). Version pins are unusually good - Trimmomatic 0.39, hisat2 2.2.1, Picard 2.0.1, MACS 1.4.2, bedtools 2.9.2, edgeR 3.34.1, karyoploteR 1.20.3, bwa 0.7.5 and 0.7.18, HiC-Pro 2.11.4, hichipper 0.7.8b0, diffloop 1.22.0, pairtools 1.1.2, samtools 1.19.2, FitHiChIP 11.0, R/RStudio 4.1 - but there is no lockfile, conda environment or container, so version stays at 1 (exact pins without environment closure). The 4 NI steps fall for distinct reasons: MACS peak calling has no parameters stated (C4), karyoploteR figure generation has no script or specification (C8), the RE-branch differential-loop step invokes DESeq2 without a version (C11), and the RAD spatial-enrichment analysis is a custom adaptation with no version and no code (C17). Because no code artifact exists to read, this paper cannot gain R-star at stage 2; the achievable ceiling remains RI.
headline.coverage: 17 computational steps assessed from Methods prose (ATAC/ChIP processing, two independent HiChIP branches, and the spatial enrichment test); 7 wet-lab steps counted (W) but out of computational-reproduction scope. Data availability is present and strong (GEO GSE312918 for new ATAC-seq, H3K27ac ChIP-seq, H3K9me3 ChIP-seq and HiChIP raw + processed data including bigwigs; GSE113192 for H3K4me3; GSE164935 for prior ATAC-seq and RNA-seq). Code availability is entirely absent.

gaps.where: All 17 computational steps (ATAC/ChIP processing, both HiChIP branches, spatial enrichment)
gaps.missing: No code repository, no scripts, no notebooks, no Makefile/workflow definition and no code-availability statement appear anywhere in the paper. The Methods prose describes tools and (for HiC-Pro and FitHiChIP) configuration values, but no executable artifact is deposited. The full-text scan for github/gitlab/bitbucket/zenodo/figshare/osf/codeocean/dryad returned only the upstream Picard documentation URL.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit an analysis repository (GitHub with a tagged release archived to Zenodo) containing the trimming/alignment/dedup/peak-calling shell scripts, the HiC-Pro and FitHiChIP configuration files as files rather than prose, the R scripts for the edgeR/DESeq2/diffloop differential-interaction analyses, the karyoploteR track-plot code, and the RAD spatial-enrichment script.

gaps.where: Software environment for all named tools and for R 4.1
gaps.missing: No conda environment file, lockfile, requirements file, or container image/digest is provided. Version pins are exact for most command-line and Bioconductor tools but there is no environment closure, so the resolved dependency set (including the R 4.1 package stack around edgeR/diffloop/DESeq2/karyoploteR) is not reconstructable. DESeq2 is invoked without any version at all.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish a conda-lock / renv.lock / pixi.lock covering the command-line tools and the full R stack, or a container image referenced by digest; record the DESeq2 version explicitly.

gaps.where: C2 modified mm10 reference; C5 'peakome' region set
gaps.missing: The mm10 reference modified to incorporate known D2 variants from Mouse Genomes Project Database REL-1505 is not deposited, and the construction procedure (variant filtering, substitution method, tooling) is not described. The 'comprehensive set of open chromatin locations (peakome)' is cited to a prior publication (ref. 28) rather than provided as a versioned BED input.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the modified reference FASTA/index (or the exact VCF plus the script that applies it) and the peakome BED file used, both with checksums, alongside the analysis repository.

gaps.where: C4 MACS peak calling; C1 Trimmomatic; C3 Picard; C8 karyoploteR
gaps.missing: MACS 1.4.2 is invoked with no parameters at all (no genome size, q/p-value cutoff, shift/extension model, or control specification). Trimmomatic adaptor set and trimming steps are unstated. Picard MarkDuplicates options are unstated. karyoploteR track parameters, window sizes and normalization for the browser-track figures are unstated, and the tool used to convert filtered bwa alignments to bigwig is not named.
gaps.how_to_close: State the exact command line for each of these invocations (or provide them in the analysis repository), and name the bigwig-generation tool and its binning/normalization settings.

gaps.missing: Two structurally different differential-loop pipelines are used for the two HiChIP branches (diffloop+DESeq2 for the restriction-enzyme branch, diffloop+edgeR for the Dovetail MNase branch) at the same FDR<0.2 cutoff, but no rationale, cross-branch concordance criterion, or seed/determinism statement is given for combining their outputs into the reported conclusions.
gaps.how_to_close: Document why each branch uses a different differential model, provide the concordance analysis between branches, and state any random-seed or tie-breaking behaviour affecting the reported differential interactions.

gaps.where: Wet-lab: congenic mouse breeding and MiniMUGA genotyping, mouse ESC derivation and culture with KASP zygosity/sex genotyping, FAST-ATAC library preparation and sequencing, H3K27ac/H3K9me3 ChIP library preparation and sequencing, restriction-enzyme HiChIP library preparation and sequencing, Dovetail HiChIP MNase Kit library preparation and sequencing, 3C-qPCR
gaps.missing: Wet-lab generation and validation steps are out of scope for computational reproduction (OOS); counted in W, not verdicted. Congenic lines, cell lines and BAC control templates are stated as 'available upon request' rather than deposited, which is a materials-availability limitation but not a computational gap.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness; scope is the bioinformatic analysis.
